title: Reduce copy fanout and introduce cooperative scheduling to lower CPU↔GPU prefill/decode overhead
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Problem: Production traces show a significant fraction of tail latency and p99 token cost coming from host-side overhead during prefill + decode flows. Symptoms include: many small memcpy operations per request that fan out across threadpool workers, frequent wakeups for GPU handoff, and contention in the dispatcher that serializes kernel selection. This ticket proposes introducing a cooperative scheduling layer and a copy-elision plan to reduce per-request CPU work and context switches.

Goals:
- Reduce CPU-side memcpy volume per request by >= 40% for 2k token prefill profiles.
- Reduce host-side scheduling wakeups (syscalls/condvar wakeups) by >= 50% during peak bursts.
- Maintain or improve p50/p95 decode latency; no regression in output fidelity or token ordering.

Scope: Changes limited to host runtime (request dispatcher, staging buffers, threadpool coordination) and a small kernel-selection hint path; no model topology changes. Must be compatible with Dedicated and Hosted modes.

High-level approach:
1) Staged inbox with ownership handoff: batch incoming requests into a small fixed-size ring per-GPU worker, then hand ownership (pointer swap) to the GPU-handling thread to avoid per-request copies.
2) Copy-elision lanes: detect when request buffers are already I/O-aligned and on pinned pages; avoid intermediate staging and instead pass scatter-gather descriptors to the DMA abstraction.
3) Cooperative scheduler: replace unconditional thread wakeups with a cooperative yield/steal protocol between the host acceptor threads and GPU worker threads to aggregate small memcopies into fewer larger DMA ops.
4) Kernel-selection hints: expose a cheap-to-evaluate heuristic (sequence-length bucket + attention type) to pre-select kernel families so GPU worker threads don't block on a slow scheduler during handoff.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Using ownership handoff increases per-ring memory footprint but dramatically reduces per-request memcpy and locks. Memory overhead bounded by ring size (configurable).
- Cooperative scheduling reduces latency variability at the cost of slightly higher average latency under very low load (we will open an opt-in flag for canary).
- DMA descriptor paths add complexity for non-PCIe platforms and must gracefully fall back to memcpy.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Phase 1 (Spike, 3 days): microbench DMA descriptor path and verify zero-copy path for small (<=4kB) and large (>64kB) buffers. Create perf harness. (Assignee: Aisha)
- Phase 2 (PoC, 5 days): implement per-GPU ring + ownership handoff and cooperative yield protocol in staging. Add metrics for memcopy_bytes, wakeups/sec, stolen_tasks/sec. (Assignee: Aisha + Marco)
- Phase 3 (Integration, 6 days): wire kernel-selection hints into runtime; add unit tests and stress test in QEMU and AWS p4dn. (Assignee: Team)
- Phase 4 (Canary, 7 days): deploy behind runtime-1.21 feature flag for 5% of traffic on hosted and one Dedicated customer cluster. Collect telemetry for 2 weeks.

Metrics to track:
- memcopy_bytes_per_request (goal -40%)
- host_wakeups_per_request (goal -50%)
- p50/p95 decode latency
- throughput (tokens/sec per GPU)
- fallback rate (zero-copy -> memcpy)

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag and run CI with extended stress tests.
2) Canary on internal infra and a low-volume Dedicated cluster for 72 hours.
3) Evaluate metrics and customer feedback; if good, expand to 20% then 100% with staggered ramp.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for ring ownership transitions and descriptor lifecycle.
- Fuzzer for interleaved handoffs to catch race conditions.
- Perf harness synthetic traces (short chat, long document prefill) and real request replay from anonymized production traces.

Risks and mitigation:
- Race conditions during ownership handoff: mitigate with formalized state machine and model checking on the fuzzer.
- Unexpected DMA failures on certain kernels: auto-fallback and increased logging to capture descriptor errors.
- Slight p50 latency regression under tiny load: keep a conservative cooperative-window default and expose config.

Open questions:
- Should ring size be per-GPU or per-device-worker? (Default: per-GPU ring to simplify affinity.)
- How to expose kernel-selection heuristic continuity across model family changes? (Plan: store per-model seed heuristics in model metadata and tie to model-version.)

Related artifacts and links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Copy+Elision+and+Cooperative+Scheduler (draft)
- Perf harness: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/perf/zero_copy_harness (WIP)

comments: 2026-03-01 - Marco Chen: Spike started. Verified DMA descriptor prototype can describe two-chain scatter/gather entries and submit via kernel ioctl in our perf harness. Initial numbers promising: small-batch memcpy reduced by ~35% in synthetic run.

2026-03-03 - Aisha Patel: Implemented per-GPU ring buffer and ownership swap. Added memcopy_bytes metric. Observed reduced locks in local test; however saw a rare double-free when a request canceled during handoff — adding extra lifecycle guard.

2026-03-06 - Marco Chen: Added cooperative yield primitive; replaced one condvar wakeup path with yield and defer. Wakeups/sec dropped ~48% in load test with 500 concurrent connections. Recording logs and adding more asserts.
2026-03-09 - QA (Jorge Alvarez): Stress run on p4dn.24xlarge: p95 improved by 12% on long-prefill workload, but token throughput dropped 3% under idle-signal scenario. Flagging for canary tuning.
2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Merged PoC behind feature flag runtime-1.21/zero_copy_coop_scheduler. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1182. Scheduling canary for 5% tomorrow.
2026-03-12 - Marco Chen: Added follow-up subtask to monitor kernel-selection mispredicts and fallback rate: ENG-96210 (will create separate ticket).
